passage: Most of the adult reed warblers that ornithologist Shahlo Bekova tracked left the marsh in late August, just as she had predicted. The young ______ stayed nearly three weeks longer, feeding heavily before their first migration.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
Here “however” interrupts a single clause, “The young birds … stayed nearly three weeks longer,” rather than joining two clauses. An interrupting word like this is set off by a pair of commas, so choice A is correct.

Choice B puts a semicolon after “birds,” but “The young birds” is not an independent clause. Choice C puts a semicolon between the subject and its verb, “stayed.” Choice D omits the comma before “however,” so the interruption is not properly set off.
explanation_uz:
Bu yerda “however” ikki gapni bog‘lamaydi, balki bitta gapni — “The young birds … stayed nearly three weeks longer” ni — bo‘lib turadi. Bunday kirish so‘z ikki tomondan vergul bilan ajratiladi, shuning uchun A to‘g‘ri.

B “birds” dan keyin nuqtali vergul qo‘yadi, lekin “The young birds” mustaqil gap emas. C ega bilan kesim (“stayed”) orasiga nuqtali vergul qo‘yadi. D “however” dan oldingi vergulni tushirib qoldiradi, shuning uchun kirish so‘z to‘liq ajratilmaydi.

passage: Every evening for six weeks, ecologist Oydin Saparova recorded the calls of frogs at a pond near her field station. Most of the calls came from a single species of tree ______ loudest choruses always began within twenty minutes of sunset.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Most of the calls came from a single species of tree frog” and “the loudest choruses always began …” are both independent clauses. Choice A is correct because a period separates them.

Choice B joins the two clauses with only a comma (a comma splice). Choice C joins them with no punctuation (a run-on sentence). Choice D is also a comma splice: “also” is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction, so it cannot join two independent clauses after a comma.
explanation_uz:
“Most of the calls came from a single species of tree frog” va “the loudest choruses always began …” — ikkalasi ham mustaqil gap. A to‘g‘ri, chunki ularni nuqta ajratadi.

B ikki gapni faqat vergul bilan bog‘laydi (comma splice). C ularni hech qanday belgisiz qo‘shib yuboradi (run-on). D ham comma splice: “also” — ravish, bog‘lovchi emas, shuning uchun verguldan keyin ikki mustaqil gapni bog‘lay olmaydi.

passage: Botanist Sevara Mirzayeva expected traffic noise to have no effect on the wildflowers she planted along a busy highway. Her results surprised ______ plants in the noisiest plots flowered nearly a week earlier than identical plants in quiet plots.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Her results surprised her” is an independent clause, and the clause after the blank explains what was surprising. A colon can introduce such an explanation after an independent clause, so choice C is correct.

Choice A joins two independent clauses with only a comma (a comma splice). Choice B is a run-on sentence. Choice D places an extra comma after “and,” which incorrectly separates the conjunction from the clause it introduces.
explanation_uz:
“Her results surprised her” — mustaqil gap, bo‘sh joydan keyingi gap esa nimasi kutilmagan bo‘lganini tushuntiradi. Mustaqil gapdan keyin bunday izohni ikki nuqta bilan boshlash mumkin, shuning uchun C to‘g‘ri.

A ikki mustaqil gapni faqat vergul bilan bog‘laydi (comma splice). B — run-on. D “and” dan keyin ortiqcha vergul qo‘yib, bog‘lovchini u boshlab berayotgan gapdan noto‘g‘ri ajratadi.

passage: The seed library at an agricultural college in Samarkand sorts its collection by the conditions each variety tolerates: drought-resistant grains, including two sorghums collected in ______ cold-hardy vegetables, such as a turnip from a village high in the mountains; and salt-tolerant herbs.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The list after the colon has three items, and the first two contain internal commas (“drought-resistant grains, including …”; “cold-hardy vegetables, such as …”). The text already uses a semicolon before “and salt-tolerant herbs,” so the first item must also end with a semicolon. Choice C is correct.

Choice A's comma blurs the line between the first item and the second, making “cold-hardy vegetables” look like a third example of drought-resistant grains. Choice B adds a second colon inside the list. Choice D runs the first item into the second.
explanation_uz:
Ikki nuqtadan keyingi ro‘yxatda uchta band bor, birinchi ikkitasining ichida vergul mavjud (“drought-resistant grains, including …”; “cold-hardy vegetables, such as …”). Matnda “and salt-tolerant herbs” dan oldin allaqachon nuqtali vergul ishlatilgan, demak birinchi band ham nuqtali vergul bilan tugashi kerak. C to‘g‘ri.

A dagi vergul birinchi va ikkinchi band orasidagi chegarani yo‘qotadi, “cold-hardy vegetables” qurg‘oqchilikka chidamli donlarning yana bir misoli kabi ko‘rinib qoladi. B ro‘yxat ichiga ikkinchi ikki nuqtani qo‘yadi. D birinchi bandni ikkinchisiga qo‘shib yuboradi.

passage: Volunteers in a city park expected the twenty bat boxes they had installed in May to be occupied within a month. What surprised the volunteers who had built and mounted the ______ that the first bats did not move in until the following summer.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The entire noun clause “What surprised the volunteers who had built and mounted the boxes” is the subject of the second sentence, and “was” is its verb. Because no punctuation goes between a subject and its verb, however long the subject is, choice C is correct.

Choice A's comma splits the subject from the verb; the length of the subject makes this error tempting. Choice B's colon and choice D's semicolon both require a complete independent clause before them, and the subject alone is not one.
explanation_uz:
“What surprised the volunteers who had built and mounted the boxes” degan butun ot ergash gap ikkinchi gapning egasi, “was” esa uning kesimi. Ega qanchalik uzun bo‘lmasin, u bilan kesim orasiga tinish belgisi qo‘yilmaydi, shuning uchun C to‘g‘ri.

A dagi vergul egani kesimdan ajratadi; eganing uzunligi bu xatoni jozibali qiladi. B dagi ikki nuqta ham, D dagi nuqtali vergul ham oldidan to‘liq mustaqil gap talab qiladi, ega o‘zi esa mustaqil gap emas.

passage: Historian Farrux Azimov's new book about Khiva begins by asking why so many nineteenth-century travelers described the city's walls as ______ traces the answer to the yellow loess clay from which the walls were built.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The first sentence reports a question indirectly (“begins by asking why … travelers described the city's walls as golden”); it is a statement, not a direct question, so it ends with a period. The words after the blank form a new independent clause. Choice C is correct.

Choice A uses a question mark, which belongs only after a direct question. Choice B is a comma splice, and choice D is a run-on sentence.
explanation_uz:
Birinchi gap savolni bilvosita yetkazadi (“begins by asking why … travelers described the city's walls as golden”); bu to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri savol emas, darak gap, shuning uchun nuqta bilan tugaydi. Bo‘sh joydan keyingi so‘zlar yangi mustaqil gap. C to‘g‘ri.

A so‘roq belgisini qo‘yadi, u esa faqat to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri savoldan keyin keladi. B — comma splice, D — run-on.

passage: Glassblowers never let a finished vase cool slowly in one spot and quickly in another. The surface of hot glass hardens before its core ______ moved promptly into an annealing oven, where the temperature drops gradually, the vase would develop internal stresses and could later crack.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“The surface of hot glass hardens before its core does” is a complete sentence. The rest, “Unless moved promptly into an annealing oven …, the vase would develop internal stresses …,” is a second independent clause that begins with an introductory phrase. Choice B correctly separates the two with a period.

Choice A seems natural because “unless moved …” looks like it belongs to the first clause, but the main clause “the vase would develop …” then follows after only a comma, creating a comma splice. Choice C is a run-on sentence. Choice D has the same comma-splice problem as A.
explanation_uz:
“The surface of hot glass hardens before its core does” — to‘liq gap. Qolgan qism “Unless moved promptly into an annealing oven …, the vase would develop internal stresses …” — kirish birikmasi bilan boshlanadigan ikkinchi mustaqil gap. B ularni nuqta bilan to‘g‘ri ajratadi.

A tabiiy ko‘rinadi, chunki “unless moved …” birinchi gapga tegishlidek tuyuladi, lekin keyin bosh gap “the vase would develop …” faqat vergul bilan keladi va comma splice hosil bo‘ladi. C — run-on. D da ham A dagi kabi comma splice muammosi bor.

passage: To protect her tomato seedlings from the cold nights of early April, gardener Zulfiya Ergasheva relies on three simple ______ plastic bottles filled with warm water, sheets of old newspaper, and a thick layer of straw around each stem.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Gardener Zulfiya Ergasheva relies on three simple tools” is a complete independent clause, and the words after the blank list those three tools. A colon correctly introduces a list after an independent clause, so choice D is correct.

Choice A's semicolon should join two independent clauses, but the list is not an independent clause. Choice B runs “tools” straight into the list. Choice C's comma makes the list look like a continuation of a series instead of an explanation of “three simple tools.”
explanation_uz:
“Gardener Zulfiya Ergasheva relies on three simple tools” — to‘liq mustaqil gap, bo‘sh joydan keyingi so‘zlar esa shu uch vositani sanab beradi. Mustaqil gapdan keyin ro‘yxatni ikki nuqta bilan boshlash to‘g‘ri, shuning uchun D to‘g‘ri.

A dagi nuqtali vergul ikki mustaqil gapni bog‘lashi kerak, ro‘yxat esa mustaqil gap emas. B da “tools” hech qanday belgisiz ro‘yxatga qo‘shilib ketadi. C dagi vergul ro‘yxatni “three simple tools” ning izohi emas, oddiy sanashning davomi kabi ko‘rsatadi.

passage: Travelers who stopped at the old caravanserai often wrote about how comfortable it was. Because its walls were made of thick mud ______ rooms inside stayed cool even during the hottest afternoons of July.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Because its walls were made of thick mud brick” is a dependent clause; it cannot stand alone. It must be attached to the main clause “the rooms inside stayed cool …” with a comma, so choice A is correct.

Choices B and C cut the dependent clause off with a period or a semicolon, leaving the fragment “Because its walls were made of thick mud brick.” Choice D adds “and,” which wrongly tries to coordinate a dependent clause with an independent one.
explanation_uz:
“Because its walls were made of thick mud brick” — ergash gap, u mustaqil tura olmaydi. U bosh gap “the rooms inside stayed cool …” ga vergul bilan biriktirilishi kerak, shuning uchun A to‘g‘ri.

B va C ergash gapni nuqta yoki nuqtali vergul bilan ajratib, “Because its walls were made of thick mud brick” degan to‘liqsiz gap (fragment) qoldiradi. D esa “and” qo‘shib, ergash gapni mustaqil gap bilan teng bog‘lashga urinadi, bu noto‘g‘ri.

passage: Central Asian tortoises spend most of the year underground in burrows, sheltering from summer heat and winter cold. In many areas, they are active above ground for only a few months in the ______ the plants they eat are still green and full of water.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The words after the blank, “when the plants they eat are still green …,” form a dependent clause that describes “the spring.” It cannot stand alone, so it must be attached to the main clause with a comma. Choice D is correct.

Choices A and C cut the dependent clause off with a period, leaving the fragments “When the plants …” and “Which is when the plants ….” Choice B uses a semicolon, but a semicolon must have an independent clause on both sides, and “when the plants they eat are still green” is not independent.
explanation_uz:
Bo‘sh joydan keyingi “when the plants they eat are still green …” — “the spring” ni izohlovchi ergash gap. U mustaqil tura olmaydi, shuning uchun bosh gapga vergul bilan biriktiriladi. D to‘g‘ri.

A va C ergash gapni nuqta bilan ajratib, “When the plants …” va “Which is when the plants …” kabi to‘liqsiz gaplar qoldiradi. B nuqtali vergul ishlatadi, lekin uning ikki tomonida ham mustaqil gap bo‘lishi kerak, “when the plants they eat are still green” esa mustaqil emas.

passage: Kamola Yusupova's grandfather, a retired railway ______ kept handwritten records of every train that passed through his small station for forty-one years. Yusupova used those notebooks to write a history of the line.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The phrase “a retired railway engineer” is a nonessential appositive that renames “Kamola Yusupova's grandfather.” It opens with a comma, so it must close with a comma too. Choice B is correct.

Choice A leaves the appositive open, so “engineer kept” runs together. Choice C's semicolon would split the subject from its verb, “kept.” Choice D closes with a dash, but the appositive opened with a comma; a pair must use matching marks.
explanation_uz:
“a retired railway engineer” — “Kamola Yusupova's grandfather” ni boshqacha nomlaydigan qo‘shimcha (nonessential) izoh. U vergul bilan boshlangan, demak vergul bilan yopilishi ham kerak. B to‘g‘ri.

A izohni yopmay qoldiradi va “engineer kept” qo‘shilib ketadi. C dagi nuqtali vergul egani kesim (“kept”) dan ajratib qo‘yadi. D izohni tire bilan yopadi, lekin izoh vergul bilan ochilgan; juft belgilar bir xil bo‘lishi kerak.

passage: The stone irrigation channels in the hillside village, which some families still use to water their walnut ______ cut by hand in the eighteenth century, according to records kept at the village mosque.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The clause “which some families still use to water their walnut orchards” is nonessential; it begins with a comma, so it must end with a comma before the main verb, “were cut.” Choice D is correct. The past-tense “were” also fits “in the eighteenth century.”

Choice A closes the clause correctly but uses the present tense “are,” which conflicts with “in the eighteenth century.” Choice B's semicolon separates the subject from its verb. Choice C closes a comma-opened clause with a dash, so the marks do not match.
explanation_uz:
“which some families still use to water their walnut orchards” — qo‘shimcha (nonessential) ergash gap; u vergul bilan boshlangan, demak asosiy kesim “were cut” dan oldin vergul bilan yopilishi kerak. D to‘g‘ri. O‘tgan zamondagi “were” “in the eighteenth century” ga ham mos keladi.

A gapni to‘g‘ri yopadi, lekin hozirgi zamondagi “are” ni ishlatadi, bu “in the eighteenth century” ga zid. B dagi nuqtali vergul egani kesimdan ajratadi. C vergul bilan ochilgan qismni tire bilan yopadi, belgilar mos emas.

passage: A youth chess federation has shortlisted three cities to host next year's national championship: Nukus, the capital of ______ Termez, near the border with Afghanistan; and Namangan, in the Fergana Valley.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
Each item in this list already contains a comma (“Nukus, the capital of Karakalpakstan”; “Termez, near the border …”). When list items contain internal commas, the items are separated by semicolons, as the text already does after “Afghanistan.” Choice B is correct.

Choice A uses a comma, which makes it impossible to tell where one city's description ends and the next item begins. Choice C adds a second colon inside the list. Choice D runs “Karakalpakstan” directly into “Termez.”
explanation_uz:
Bu ro‘yxatning har bir bandida allaqachon vergul bor (“Nukus, the capital of Karakalpakstan”; “Termez, near the border …”). Bandlar ichida vergul bo‘lsa, bandlar o‘zaro nuqtali vergul bilan ajratiladi — matnda “Afghanistan” dan keyin ham shunday qilingan. B to‘g‘ri.

A vergul ishlatadi, natijada bir shahar tavsifi qayerda tugab, keyingi band qayerda boshlanishini bilib bo‘lmaydi. C ro‘yxat ichiga ikkinchi ikki nuqtani qo‘yadi. D “Karakalpakstan” ni “Termez” ga to‘g‘ridan-to‘g‘ri qo‘shib yuboradi.

passage: At the bird-ringing station on the mountain pass, volunteers start work before sunrise. Each morning, they check the fine nets strung across the ______ record the species, weight, and wing length of every bird caught before releasing it.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The sentence has one subject, “they,” and two verbs, “check” and “record.” Two verbs that share a subject form a compound predicate, and no comma is needed before “and” in that case. Choice A is correct.

Choice B adds a comma that separates the second verb from its subject, as if “record …” were an independent clause. Choice C creates the fragment “And record the species ….” Choice D's semicolon also requires an independent clause after it, but “and record the species …” has no subject.
explanation_uz:
Gapda bitta ega (“they”) va ikkita kesim (“check” va “record”) bor. Bir egaga tegishli ikki fe’l uyushiq kesim hosil qiladi, bunda “and” dan oldin vergul kerak emas. A to‘g‘ri.

B ikkinchi fe’lni egasidan ajratuvchi vergul qo‘shadi, go‘yo “record …” mustaqil gapdek. C “And record the species …” degan to‘liqsiz gap hosil qiladi. D dagi nuqtali vergul ham undan keyin mustaqil gap talab qiladi, “and record the species …” da esa ega yo‘q.

passage: Dilfuza Abdullaeva opened her bakery in Andijan in 1985, and today she runs it with her three sons. The bakery's best seller, a round flatbread topped with nigella seeds, was invented by her ______ when he was just sixteen.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The text says Abdullaeva has three sons, so the name “Jahongir” is essential: it tells which son invented the bread. An essential appositive is not set off with commas, so choice A is correct.

Choice B sets the name off as nonessential, which would imply she has only one son and contradicts “her three sons.” Choice C opens a comma but never closes it. Choice D's semicolon cuts the clause apart, leaving “Jahongir when he was just sixteen” as a fragment.
explanation_uz:
Matnda Abdullaevaning uchta o‘g‘li borligi aytilgan, demak “Jahongir” ismi zarur (essential): u nonni qaysi o‘g‘il o‘ylab topganini bildiradi. Zarur izoh vergul bilan ajratilmaydi, shuning uchun A to‘g‘ri.

B ismni qo‘shimcha (nonessential) izoh sifatida ajratadi, bu esa uning faqat bitta o‘g‘li bordek ko‘rsatadi va “her three sons” ga zid. C vergul ochadi, lekin yopmaydi. D dagi nuqtali vergul gapni bo‘lib, “Jahongir when he was just sixteen” ni to‘liqsiz gap holida qoldiradi.

passage: Engineers at the textile mill expected the new looms to cut the mill's electricity use by a third. After a year of operation, the savings were closer to a ______ looms broke down so rarely that repair costs fell even more than predicted.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“The savings were closer to a quarter” and “the looms broke down so rarely …” are both independent clauses, and “however” introduces the second one. A conjunctive adverb that begins the second clause is preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma, so choice D is correct.

Choice A is a comma splice; “however” cannot join two clauses after a comma. Choice B has no punctuation at all. Choice C places the semicolon after “however,” which wrongly attaches the contrast word to the first clause.
explanation_uz:
“The savings were closer to a quarter” va “the looms broke down so rarely …” — ikkalasi ham mustaqil gap, “however” esa ikkinchisini boshlaydi. Ikkinchi gapni boshlovchi bog‘lovchi ravishdan oldin nuqtali vergul, keyin vergul qo‘yiladi, shuning uchun D to‘g‘ri.

A — comma splice; “however” verguldan keyin ikki gapni bog‘lay olmaydi. B da umuman tinish belgisi yo‘q. C nuqtali vergulni “however” dan keyin qo‘yib, qarama-qarshilik so‘zini birinchi gapga noto‘g‘ri biriktiradi.

passage: The city's transport office has studied bus traffic on its busiest routes for two years. Its final report, released to the public last ______ that the city replace three of its oldest routes with a single express line.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The phrase “released to the public last month” gives extra information about “Its final report.” It opens with a comma, so it must also close with a comma before the verb “recommends.” Choice C is correct.

Choice A leaves the phrase unclosed. Choice B's semicolon separates the subject, “Its final report,” from its verb. Choice D closes a comma-opened phrase with a dash, so the marks do not match.
explanation_uz:
“released to the public last month” — “Its final report” haqida qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. U vergul bilan ochilgan, demak “recommends” fe’lidan oldin vergul bilan yopilishi ham kerak. C to‘g‘ri.

A birikmani yopmay qoldiradi. B dagi nuqtali vergul egani (“Its final report”) kesimdan ajratadi. D vergul bilan ochilgan birikmani tire bilan yopadi, belgilar mos emas.

passage: The oldest photographs in the city archive, taken in the 1880s, show market scenes that have since vanished, ______ a row of tinsmiths' stalls, a bread oven built into the city wall, and a camel caravan unloading bales of cotton.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Including” introduces the examples and connects directly to them; the list is its object. No punctuation belongs between “including” and the items that follow, so choice D is correct.

Choice A is a common mistake: a colon must follow a complete independent clause, and a phrase ending in “including” is not one. Choice B's semicolon would need an independent clause on each side. Choice C places a comma between “including” and its object for no reason.
explanation_uz:
“Including” misollarni boshlab beradi va ularga bevosita bog‘lanadi; ro‘yxat uning to‘ldiruvchisi. “Including” bilan undan keyingi bandlar orasiga tinish belgisi qo‘yilmaydi, shuning uchun D to‘g‘ri.

A — keng tarqalgan xato: ikki nuqta to‘liq mustaqil gapdan keyin kelishi kerak, “including” bilan tugaydigan qism esa mustaqil gap emas. B dagi nuqtali vergul ikki tomonda ham mustaqil gap talab qiladi. C “including” bilan uning to‘ldiruvchisi orasiga sababsiz vergul qo‘yadi.

passage: Founded in 1961 by a group of retired ______ town's amateur astronomy club still meets on the first Friday of every month. Its members gather on the flat roof of the old post office, where a donated telescope stands under a canvas cover.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Founded in 1961 by a group of retired schoolteachers” is an introductory participial phrase that describes the club; it is not a complete sentence. A comma should separate it from the main clause, “the town's amateur astronomy club still meets …,” so choice B is correct.

Choice A omits the comma, so “schoolteachers the town's …” runs together confusingly. Choices C and D cut the phrase off with a period or a semicolon, leaving “Founded in 1961 by a group of retired schoolteachers” as a fragment.
explanation_uz:
“Founded in 1961 by a group of retired schoolteachers” — klubni tasvirlovchi kirish sifatdosh birikma, u to‘liq gap emas. Uni bosh gap “the town's amateur astronomy club still meets …” dan vergul bilan ajratish kerak, shuning uchun B to‘g‘ri.

A vergulni tushirib qoldiradi va “schoolteachers the town's …” chalkash qo‘shilib ketadi. C va D birikmani nuqta yoki nuqtali vergul bilan ajratib, “Founded in 1961 by a group of retired schoolteachers” ni to‘liqsiz gap holida qoldiradi.

passage: The city council rejected the first three designs for the footbridge before approving a fourth. The final design had one feature that all of the earlier drafts had ______ a covered walkway that shelters pedestrians from both summer sun and winter snow.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“The final design had one feature that all of the earlier drafts had lacked” is a complete independent clause; “that all of the earlier drafts had lacked” describes “feature.” The words after the blank then identify that feature. A dash can introduce such an explanation after an independent clause, so choice D is correct.

Choice C is tempting because “lacked a covered walkway” sounds like a verb and its object, but “lacked” already has its object (“that,” referring to “feature”), so the sentence becomes garbled. Choice A is a comma splice. Choice B's semicolon would need an independent clause after it, and “a covered walkway that shelters …” is only a noun phrase.
explanation_uz:
“The final design had one feature that all of the earlier drafts had lacked” — to‘liq mustaqil gap; “that all of the earlier drafts had lacked” “feature” ni izohlaydi. Bo‘sh joydan keyingi so‘zlar esa o‘sha xususiyat nima ekanini aytadi. Mustaqil gapdan keyin bunday izohni tire bilan boshlash mumkin, shuning uchun D to‘g‘ri.

C jozibali, chunki “lacked a covered walkway” fe’l va to‘ldiruvchidek eshitiladi, lekin “lacked” ning to‘ldiruvchisi allaqachon bor (“feature” ga ishora qiluvchi “that”), shuning uchun gap chalkashib ketadi. A — comma splice. B dagi nuqtali vergul undan keyin mustaqil gap talab qiladi, “a covered walkway that shelters …” esa faqat ot birikmasi.

passage: Most readers know the twelfth-century poem only through English translations made in the 1920s. In a new study, the literary ______ Usmonova argues that these versions miss nearly all of the poem's wordplay.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
In “the literary scholar Nodira Usmonova,” the name identifies which literary scholar is meant; it is essential, so no punctuation separates it from “scholar.” Choice A is correct.

Choices B and C open a nonessential element with a comma or a dash but never close it, so the subject is cut off from its verb, “argues.” Choice D's colon must follow an independent clause, but “In a new study, the literary scholar” is not one.
explanation_uz:
“the literary scholar Nodira Usmonova” birikmasida ism qaysi adabiyotshunos nazarda tutilganini aniqlaydi; u zarur (essential), shuning uchun “scholar” dan tinish belgisi bilan ajratilmaydi. A to‘g‘ri.

B va C vergul yoki tire bilan qo‘shimcha qism ochadi, lekin uni yopmaydi, natijada ega kesim (“argues”) dan uzilib qoladi. D dagi ikki nuqta mustaqil gapdan keyin kelishi kerak, “In a new study, the literary scholar” esa mustaqil gap emas.

passage: In many villages of the Fergana Valley, beekeepers still use traditional hives as well as modern ones. The narrow wooden boxes that some beekeepers hang from the branches of apricot ______ designed to attract wild swarms in early spring.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The subject of the second sentence is the long noun phrase “The narrow wooden boxes that some beekeepers hang from the branches of apricot trees,” and its verb is “are.” No punctuation should separate a subject from its verb, so choice C is correct.

Choices A, B, and D place a comma, a dash, or a semicolon between the subject and the verb, which wrongly splits the clause. A semicolon (D) would also need an independent clause on each side.
explanation_uz:
Ikkinchi gapning egasi — uzun ot birikmasi “The narrow wooden boxes that some beekeepers hang from the branches of apricot trees,” kesimi esa “are.” Ega bilan kesim orasiga hech qanday tinish belgisi qo‘yilmaydi, shuning uchun C to‘g‘ri.

A, B va D ega bilan kesim orasiga vergul, tire yoki nuqtali vergul qo‘yib, gapni noto‘g‘ri bo‘lib yuboradi. Nuqtali vergul (D) uchun esa ikki tomonda ham mustaqil gap bo‘lishi kerak.

passage: Agronomist Rustam Qodirov compared soil samples from twelve orchards in the same district. He ______ trees planted beside irrigation ditches had roots nearly twice as deep as trees planted farther from water.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The clause “that trees planted beside irrigation ditches had roots …” is the object of the verb “found”; it tells what he found. No punctuation belongs between a verb and its object, so choice C is correct.

Choices A, B, and D all insert a mark (a comma, a colon, or a semicolon) between “found” and the clause it needs. A colon or semicolon would also require a complete independent clause before it, and “He found” is incomplete without its object.
explanation_uz:
“that trees planted beside irrigation ditches had roots …” ergash gapi “found” fe’lining to‘ldiruvchisi; u nimani aniqlaganini bildiradi. Fe’l va uning to‘ldiruvchisi orasiga tinish belgisi qo‘yilmaydi, shuning uchun C to‘g‘ri.

A, B va D “found” bilan unga kerak bo‘lgan ergash gap orasiga belgi (vergul, ikki nuqta yoki nuqtali vergul) qo‘yadi. Ikki nuqta yoki nuqtali vergul oldidan to‘liq mustaqil gap bo‘lishi kerak, “He found” esa to‘ldiruvchisiz to‘liq emas.

passage: The regional museum's new exhibit on early printing was organized by ______ Lola Hamidova, who spent two years tracking down surviving copies of the town's first newspaper.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Curator” works here like a title placed directly before the name “Lola Hamidova.” A descriptive title right before a name is not separated from it by punctuation, so choice D is correct.

Choices A, B, and C put a comma, a colon, or a dash between “curator” and the name, which needlessly splits a single noun phrase that serves as the object of the preposition “by.”
explanation_uz:
“Curator” bu yerda “Lola Hamidova” ismidan bevosita oldin turgan unvon vazifasini bajaradi. Ism oldidagi unvon undan tinish belgisi bilan ajratilmaydi, shuning uchun D to‘g‘ri.

A, B va C “curator” bilan ism orasiga vergul, ikki nuqta yoki tire qo‘yadi. Bu “by” predlogidan keyin keladigan yagona ot birikmasini keraksiz ravishda bo‘lib yuboradi.

passage: After the spring cleanup along the canal, volunteers sorted everything they had collected into four bins: plastic bottles, glass ______ cans, and everything else.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The words after the colon form a simple list of four items: “plastic bottles,” “glass jars,” “metal cans,” and “everything else.” Items in a simple series are separated by commas, so choice B is correct.

Choice A leaves out the comma, running two items together as if “glass jars metal cans” were one item. Choice C uses a semicolon, which is used in lists only when the items themselves contain commas. Choice D adds a second colon inside the list, which is not allowed.
explanation_uz:
Ikki nuqtadan keyingi so‘zlar to‘rt bandli oddiy ro‘yxat: “plastic bottles,” “glass jars,” “metal cans” va “everything else.” Oddiy ro‘yxat bandlari vergul bilan ajratiladi, shuning uchun B to‘g‘ri.

A vergulni tushirib qoldiradi va ikki bandni bitta qilib qo‘shib yuboradi. C nuqtali vergul ishlatadi, u esa ro‘yxatda faqat bandlarning o‘zida vergul bo‘lganda qo‘llanadi. D ro‘yxat ichiga ikkinchi ikki nuqtani qo‘yadi, bu mumkin emas.

passage: Geologist Anvar Toshpo‘latov spent three summers mapping the layered red cliffs above the river. In his field journal, he wrote that the cliffs ______ “like a stack of books someone had dropped and never picked up.”
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The quotation is grammatically part of the sentence: “he wrote that the cliffs looked ‘like a stack of books …’” Because the quoted words continue the clause introduced by “that,” no punctuation is needed before them. Choice B is correct.

Choice A adds a comma that separates the verb “looked” from the phrase that completes it. Choice C's colon must follow a complete independent clause, but “that the cliffs looked” is not one. Choice D's semicolon would need an independent clause on both sides.
explanation_uz:
Iqtibos gapning grammatik qismi: “he wrote that the cliffs looked ‘like a stack of books …’” Iqtibosdagi so‘zlar “that” bilan boshlangan gapni davom ettirgani uchun ulardan oldin tinish belgisi kerak emas. B to‘g‘ri.

A “looked” fe’lini uni to‘ldiruvchi birikmadan ajratuvchi vergul qo‘shadi. C dagi ikki nuqta to‘liq mustaqil gapdan keyin kelishi kerak, “that the cliffs looked” esa mustaqil emas. D dagi nuqtali vergul uchun ikki tomonda ham mustaqil gap bo‘lishi kerak.

passage: According to a chronicle studied by historian Bobur Aliqulov, the builders of a medieval mosque hauled every block of stone from a quarry two days' walk away. Then a newly dug canal shortened the trip by almost a ______ allowed the workers to finish the outer walls years ahead of schedule.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“Then a newly dug canal shortened the trip by almost a day” and “This allowed the workers to finish …” are both independent clauses; a pronoun such as “this” can begin a new clause. Choice D correctly separates them with a period.

Choice A is a comma splice. Choice B is a run-on sentence. Choice C is still a comma splice, because “thus” is an adverb, not a coordinating conjunction.
explanation_uz:
“Then a newly dug canal shortened the trip by almost a day” va “This allowed the workers to finish …” — ikkalasi ham mustaqil gap; “this” kabi olmosh yangi gapni boshlashi mumkin. D ularni nuqta bilan to‘g‘ri ajratadi.

A — comma splice. B — run-on. C ham comma splice, chunki “thus” — ravish, teng bog‘lovchi emas.

passage: A group of students launched a weather balloon from their school's sports field, but it burst at only 9,000 meters. For their second launch, they chose a balloon made of thicker ______ new balloon climbed above 25,000 meters before bursting.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The blank sits between two independent clauses: “they chose a balloon made of thicker latex” and “the new balloon climbed above 25,000 meters.” A comma followed by the coordinating conjunction “and” correctly joins them, so choice A is correct.

Choice B puts the comma after “and” instead of before it. Choice C is a comma splice. Choice D is a run-on sentence with no punctuation or conjunction.
explanation_uz:
Bo‘sh joy ikki mustaqil gap orasida: “they chose a balloon made of thicker latex” va “the new balloon climbed above 25,000 meters.” Vergul va undan keyingi “and” bog‘lovchisi ularni to‘g‘ri bog‘laydi, shuning uchun A to‘g‘ri.

B vergulni “and” dan oldin emas, keyin qo‘yadi. C — comma splice. D da hech qanday tinish belgisi ham, bog‘lovchi ham yo‘q (run-on).

passage: Potter Behruz Nazarov fires his bowls in a wood-burning kiln that he built himself. The fire must be fed every few minutes for nearly two ______ single firing can use an entire cartload of apricot wood.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
Both “The fire must be fed every few minutes for nearly two days” and “a single firing can use an entire cartload of apricot wood” are independent clauses. A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses, so choice B is correct.

Choice A is a comma splice. Choice C is a run-on sentence with no punctuation between the clauses. Choice D is still a comma splice, because “meanwhile” is an adverb and cannot join clauses the way “and” or “so” can.
explanation_uz:
“The fire must be fed every few minutes for nearly two days” ham, “a single firing can use an entire cartload of apricot wood” ham mustaqil gap. Nuqtali vergul ma’no jihatdan yaqin ikki mustaqil gapni to‘g‘ri bog‘laydi, shuning uchun B to‘g‘ri.

A — comma splice. C — gaplar orasida hech qanday belgi yo‘q (run-on). D ham comma splice, chunki “meanwhile” — ravish, u “and” yoki “so” kabi gaplarni bog‘lay olmaydi.

passage: When the composer's only string quartet premiered, critics dismissed its abrupt final bars as a sign that she had rushed to meet a deadline. The work was not hastily ______ composer's letters show that she revised its ending eleven times over two years.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
“However” contrasts the critics' view (that the quartet was rushed) with the claim “The work was not hastily written,” so it belongs to the first clause. The second clause, “the composer's letters show …,” is independent and must be separated by a semicolon. Choice B, “written, however; the,” is correct.

Choice A is a comma splice. Choice C attaches “however” to the second clause, which wrongly sets up a contrast between “not hastily written” and the letters that support that very point; it also lacks the comma after “however.” Choice D has no punctuation between the two independent clauses.
explanation_uz:
“However” tanqidchilar fikri (kvartet shoshilib yozilgan) bilan “The work was not hastily written” degan da’voni qarama-qarshi qo‘yadi, demak u birinchi gapga tegishli. Ikkinchi gap “the composer's letters show …” mustaqil, u nuqtali vergul bilan ajratilishi kerak. B — “written, however; the” — to‘g‘ri.

A — comma splice. C “however” ni ikkinchi gapga biriktirib, “not hastily written” bilan aynan shu fikrni tasdiqlovchi maktublar o‘rtasida noto‘g‘ri qarama-qarshilik yaratadi; bundan tashqari “however” dan keyin vergul yo‘q. D da ikki mustaqil gap orasida hech qanday belgi yo‘q.

passage: The mural on the side of the old bus depot—painted in 1978 by a group of art ______ restored last summer with the help of photographs from the city archive. Several of the original painters, now in their sixties, joined the restoration team.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The phrase “painted in 1978 by a group of art students” is extra information inserted between the subject, “The mural on the side of the old bus depot,” and its verb, “was restored.” It opens with a dash, so it must close with a dash. Choice C is correct.

Choice A closes the interruption with a comma, which does not match the opening dash. Choice B's semicolon separates the subject from its verb. Choice D never closes the interruption, so the sentence reads as if the students were restored.
explanation_uz:
“painted in 1978 by a group of art students” — ega (“The mural on the side of the old bus depot”) va kesim (“was restored”) orasiga qo‘shilgan qo‘shimcha ma’lumot. U tire bilan ochilgan, demak tire bilan yopilishi kerak. C to‘g‘ri.

A qo‘shimcha qismni vergul bilan yopadi, bu ochuvchi tirega mos emas. B dagi nuqtali vergul egani kesimdan ajratadi. D qo‘shimcha qismni umuman yopmaydi, natijada gap go‘yo talabalar ta’mirlangandek o‘qiladi.

passage: The expedition's most valuable find—a palm-leaf manuscript whose pages, though stained by water and darkened with age, were still ______ carried out of the cave in a padded steel case and flown to the conservation laboratory that same week.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation_en:
The long interruption “a palm-leaf manuscript whose pages … were still legible” renames “The expedition's most valuable find” and sits between that subject and its verb, “was carried.” It opened with a dash, so it must close with a dash. Choice A is correct.

Choice B is tempting because of the commas around “though stained by water and darkened with age,” but those commas form their own completed pair; a comma here cannot close a dash-opened interruption. Choice C's semicolon separates the subject from its verb. Choice D never closes the interruption.
explanation_uz:
Uzun qo‘shimcha qism “a palm-leaf manuscript whose pages … were still legible” “The expedition's most valuable find” ni boshqacha nomlaydi va shu ega bilan kesim (“was carried”) orasida turadi. U tire bilan ochilgan, demak tire bilan yopilishi kerak. A to‘g‘ri.

B jozibali ko‘rinadi, chunki “though stained by water and darkened with age” atrofida vergullar bor, lekin ular o‘z juftini allaqachon yopgan; bu yerdagi vergul tire bilan ochilgan qismni yopa olmaydi. C dagi nuqtali vergul egani kesimdan ajratadi. D qo‘shimcha qismni umuman yopmaydi.
